summary: Aminosteril N-Hepa 8% (Fresenius Kabi Austria GmbH) is an amino acid solution enriched in branched-chain amino acids for parenteral nutrition in severe liver insufficiency, with or without hepatic encephalopathy. Philippine registration: 500 ml bottle. It is a hepatic formula, not a kidney formula.
composition_notes: No electrolytes are listed apart from acetate as lysine monoacetate; theoretical osmolarity is not stated in the short SmPC.

Source is the Austrian manufacturer short SmPC (Fachkurzinformation) of Aminosteril Hepa 8% (March 2018), in German, translated; the Philippine product is registered as Aminosteril N-Hepa 8% (80 g/l). Confirm against the Philippine package insert.
kidney_notes: Renal insufficiency is listed as a contraindication, along with hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis, shock, hypoxia and general infusion contraindications (Fachkurzinformation, contraindications).
guideline_heading: How it fits the ESPEN 2021 kidney nutrition guideline
guideline: ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 24: "No disease-specific enteral nor parenteral formula oriented for patients with reduced kidney function should be routinely utilized in every patient with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF in comparison to conventional formulas. Instead, their use is to be individualized (see recommendation 26)." Grade of recommendation B – Consensus (87.5% agreement). (AKI, acute kidney injury; CKD, chronic kidney disease; KF, kidney failure.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 31: "Electrolytes abnormalities are common in patients with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF receiving KRT and shall be closely monitored." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (100% agreement). (KRT, kidney replacement therapy.)
bottom_line: A hepatic (branched-chain-enriched) amino acid solution. The available SmPC lists renal insufficiency as a contraindication, so it is not a choice for a patient with kidney failure unless the current Philippine insert says otherwise; for hepatorenal patients, involve the nutrition team.
withheld: Maximum daily dose and infusion rate (not in the short SmPC).
Full special warnings (the short SmPC refers to the full Fachinformation).
